title.title: Infinite matroid intersection and packing/covering fail
title.subtitle: Claim: two self-dual matroids on a countable set admit no packing/covering partition and no intersection

plain: Matroids capture what 'independent' means; for infinite ones, a classic matching theorem breaks

panels.caption: copies of one self-dual uniform matroid $Q$, along a doubly infinite path

lines.tex: \nexists\ I_0 \cup I_1 = E,\ \ I_j \text{ independent in } M_j

beats.text: One self-dual uniform matroid $Q$, built with an ultrafilter, copied along a path
Covering the ground set by two independent sets would make an ordinal descend forever
So infinite intersection and packing/covering fail, in ZFC

steps: Build a self-dual matroid from an ultrafilter rank
Chain copies along a path: any cover makes the rank drop
Ranks can't drop forever, so no cover exists

achievement.label: Infinite matroid intersection and packing/covering conjectures
statement: \text{every pair } M_0, M_1 \text{ has a packing/covering partition}
achievement.context: Two self-dual partitional matroids on a countable set; neither finitary nor cofinitary
achievement.note: Nash-Williams' original finitary conjecture is untouched

verify.detail: Countable $E$, two self-dual matroids, no covering and no partition; Mathlib's matroids
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean statement; we did not build it

voice.text: Edmonds' theorem holds for finite matroids. Does it survive the jump to infinite ones?
Any cover would force an ordinal rank to drop forever, and that cannot happen.

sources.quote: both self-dual and partitional (countable direct sums of one self-dual uniform matroid Q), such that no independent I0 of M0 and I1 of M1 cover E
then places copies along a doubly infinite path so that any attempt to cover the ground set by two independent sets must 'descend' forever in ordinal rank
Examples are neither finitary nor cofinitary.
so Nash-Williams' original finitary conjecture is untouched
It is formalized using Mathlib's infinite matroids
